eng-block.does: The 2.0L four-cylinder Zetec itself: iron block, aluminum twin-cam head, the assembly that burns fuel and spins the crank.
eng-block.fails: Blue smoke, oil use, knocking, low compression, or coolant in the oil mean the core engine, not a bolt-on, is worn.
eng-block.tip: Rarely replaced; fix leaks and keep the timing belt current. A used Zetec swap is cheaper than a rebuild.

valve-cover.does: The lid on top of the engine covering the camshafts; its rubber gasket keeps oil in.
valve-cover.fails: Oil smell after driving, oil wet around the top of the engine or dripping down the back, sometimes oil in the spark plug wells.
valve-cover.tip: Zetec gasket is YS4Z-6584-AA / Fel-Pro VS 50581 R; bolts are low torque (about 5 ft-lb), do not crank them down.

timing-belt.does: Toothed rubber belt that keeps the two camshafts in step with the crankshaft so valves and pistons never meet.
timing-belt.fails: Usually no warning; a tick or squeal from the belt cover, then a sudden no-start with a fast, easy crank means it broke and valves are bent.
timing-belt.tip: Change every 100k miles or 8 years with tensioner and idler (Gates TCK294 kit). Interference engine: do not gamble on it.

oil-pan.does: Steel tub bolted under the engine that holds the oil supply the pump draws from.
oil-pan.fails: Oil drips under the front of the car after parking, a rusty or dented pan, or a stripped drain plug that will not stop weeping.
oil-pan.tip: Zetec pan (YS4Z-6675-AA) seals with RTV, not a paper gasket; clean both faces fully. Drain plug torque about 18 ft-lb.

oil-filter.does: Screws onto the block and strains dirt and metal out of the oil every time it circulates.
oil-filter.fails: Nothing you will feel until it is badly clogged; the symptom is dirty oil and, in time, engine wear.
oil-filter.tip: Motorcraft FL-400S; hand tight plus three-quarter turn. Change with every oil change (about 5k miles on conventional oil).

motor-mounts.does: Rubber and fluid-filled blocks that hold the engine and transaxle to the body and soak up vibration.
motor-mounts.fails: Clunk or thump on takeoff and when shifting between drive and reverse, engine visibly rocking, more vibration at idle.
motor-mounts.tip: The hydraulic right-side (passenger) mount is the usual failure; look for fluid weeping from it. Support the engine before unbolting.

serp-belt.does: One long ribbed belt off the crank pulley that spins the alternator, water pump, power steering pump and A/C compressor.
serp-belt.fails: Squeal on cold start or when turning the wheel, cracks across the ribs, or a battery light and hot engine if it snaps.
serp-belt.tip: 6-rib K060882 with A/C; the spring tensioner (YS4Z-6B209-AA) weakens, so replace it with the belt. Photograph the routing first.

spark-plugs.does: Four plugs make the spark in each cylinder; the coil pack on the head boosts 12 volts to the thousands needed to jump the gap.
spark-plugs.fails: Rough idle, shaking, hesitation, flashing check engine light with a misfire code for one cylinder.
spark-plugs.tip: Plug AZFS-32F-E gapped 0.052 in, torque about 11 ft-lb. Coil XS8Z-12029-AA; cracked coils fail wet, so suspect it after rain.

radiator.does: The finned block behind the grille where air pulls heat out of the coolant.
radiator.fails: Sweet smell, crust or damp at the plastic end tanks, temp gauge creeping up on the highway, low coolant with no visible leak.
radiator.tip: Spectra CU2296 / 3S4Z-8005-GA. Plastic end tanks crack with age; the automatic's fluid cooler is in one tank. Refill with Motorcraft Gold.

rad-fan.does: Electric fan behind the radiator that pulls air through when the car is not moving fast enough to do it.
rad-fan.fails: Temp gauge climbs at idle or in traffic but is fine on the highway; A/C blows warm at a stop.
rad-fan.tip: Test by switching A/C on: the fan should run. Check the fan relay and fuse in the engine bay box before buying a motor.

thermostat.does: A wax valve in a plastic housing that holds coolant in the engine until it is warm, then lets it out to the radiator.
thermostat.fails: Heater slow to warm and gauge sits low (stuck open), sudden overheat (stuck closed), or the plastic housing cracks and leaks.
thermostat.tip: Buy housing and thermostat together (YS4Z-8592-BD); the old plastic housing is a known weak point. Drain some coolant first.

water-pump.does: Belt-driven pump on the side of the block that circulates coolant through the engine and radiator.
water-pump.fails: Coolant weep from the small hole under the pump, a grinding or rumbling bearing noise, or overheating.
water-pump.tip: On the Zetec it runs off the serpentine belt, not the timing belt, so it is a stand-alone job. YS4Z-8501-AA or Gates 42294.

rad-hoses.does: Two big rubber hoses carrying coolant between the engine and the radiator, hot going out, cooler coming back.
rad-hoses.fails: Hose feels mushy or crunchy, bulges near the clamps, or wets the area around the ends; a burst hose empties the system fast.
rad-hoses.tip: Squeeze them cold; swap both at once (Motorcraft KM-4590 upper, Gates 22500 lower). Fresh clamps and Motorcraft Gold coolant.

coolant-res.does: The pressurized plastic tank on top that you fill, where air separates out of the coolant; its cap sets system pressure.
coolant-res.fails: Hairline cracks that weep, level that keeps dropping, brown stains on the tank, or a cap that will not hold pressure.
coolant-res.tip: Known weak point; replace at the first crack (3S4Z-8A080-AC) and buy a new cap with it. Never open it hot.

intake-mani.does: Runners on the back of the head that split incoming air into four equal streams, one per cylinder.
intake-mani.fails: Vacuum hiss, high or hunting idle, lean code P0171 from a leaking gasket or a cracked runner.
intake-mani.tip: Check the gaskets and the PCV and brake booster hoses that plug into it first; a leak there mimics a bad manifold.

throttle-body.does: The butterfly valve your gas pedal opens by cable to let air into the engine.
throttle-body.fails: Rough or low idle, stalling at stops, sticky pedal feel from a carbon-caked bore.
throttle-body.tip: Cleaning fixes most complaints: throttle body cleaner on a rag, wipe the bore and plate. Verify the part by VIN if replacing.

airbox.does: Plastic box holding the paper air filter that keeps dust out of the engine.
airbox.fails: Sluggish power and worse fuel economy as the filter clogs; a torn filter lets grit past to the MAF and engine.
airbox.tip: Check yearly, change every 15-30k miles. Motorcraft FA-1632 or K&N 33-2819 drop-in; snap every clip back on.

maf.does: Hot-wire sensor in the intake tube that measures how much air is entering so the PCM can add matching fuel.
maf.fails: Hesitation, stumble on takeoff, rough idle, poor mileage, lean or rich codes; often after an over-oiled aftermarket filter.
maf.tip: Try MAF-specific cleaner spray first and never touch the wires. Unplug the battery a few minutes afterward to reset the PCM.

fuel-inj.does: Four electric spray nozzles on a metal rail that mist gasoline into each intake port on command from the PCM.
fuel-inj.fails: Misfire on one cylinder that does not follow the coil, gas smell under the hood, rough idle.
fuel-inj.tip: Depressurize the fuel line first. Replace the O-rings when you pull the rail; a bottle of injector cleaner is worth a try before parts.

fuel-pump.does: Electric pump inside the gas tank that pushes fuel forward to the engine at pressure.
fuel-pump.fails: Long cranking, stalling when hot or uphill, loss of power under load, a whine from under the rear seat.
fuel-pump.tip: Access is under the rear seat cushion, no tank drop. Run the tank low first, and keep it above a quarter to keep the pump cool.

fuel-tank.does: 13.2-gallon plastic tank under the rear seat area that stores the gasoline and houses the pump.
fuel-tank.fails: Fuel smell at the back, evap code P0455 from a bad seal, or a leak after hitting road debris.
fuel-tank.tip: Plastic tanks do not rust; most 'tank' smells are the filler neck, pump ring seal or the gas cap. Check the cap first.

fuel-filter.does: Canister filter under the car that strains rust and dirt from gasoline before it reaches the injectors.
fuel-filter.fails: Hesitation and power loss under load, or long cranks, as it clogs.
fuel-filter.tip: Motorcraft FG-986B; needs the plastic quick-connect tool and the arrow points toward the engine. Eye protection, fuel will spill.

pcv.does: A one-way valve and hose that pull oily crankcase vapor back into the intake to be burned instead of vented.
pcv.fails: Oil leaks from gaskets and seals from crankcase pressure, oil in the intake, rough idle, oil use.
pcv.tip: Cheap part: shake it and it should rattle. Check the rubber hose for softening or collapse; a split hose is a vacuum leak.

alternator.does: Belt-driven generator that recharges the battery and powers everything electrical once the engine is running.
alternator.fails: Battery light, dimming dash, headlights that pulse with engine speed, dead battery after a drive, whine or growl from the front.
alternator.tip: Lester 8260 for this car, not 8418 or 8406. Confirm belt tension and the battery first: many 'alternators' are a slipping belt.

starter.does: Small motor that engages the flywheel to spin the engine over when you turn the key.
starter.fails: Click but no crank, slow crank with a good battery, or grinding noise at start.
starter.tip: Manual and automatic use different starters; know which transaxle you have. Disconnect the battery negative before touching it.

battery.does: Group 96R lead-acid battery that stores power to start the car and steady the electrical system.
battery.fails: Slow crank on cold mornings, click-click at the key, needs a jump, dash flicker; most last 4-5 years.
battery.tip: Motorcraft BXT-96R-590 fits. Clean terminals with baking soda; the PCM relearns idle after a disconnect, so a rough idle for a day is normal.

ignition-sw.does: The lock cylinder your key turns and the electrical switch behind it that wakes the car and cranks the starter.
ignition-sw.fails: Key hard to turn or sticks, car dies when the key is jiggled, no crank on some tries, dash flicker.
ignition-sw.tip: Switch and cylinder are separate parts. A new cylinder means new keys, so plan on PATS programming; disconnect the battery (airbag).

o2-sensors.does: Two sensors in the exhaust that report how rich or lean the burn is; upstream trims fuel, downstream grades the converter.
o2-sensors.fails: Poor mileage, rough idle, check engine light with O2 or catalyst codes, failed emissions test.
o2-sensors.tip: Penetrant on the threads and an O2 socket while the exhaust is warm. Fix exhaust leaks first; a leak fools the sensor.

ckp-sensor.does: Magnetic sensor beside the crank pulley that tells the PCM exactly where the engine is in its rotation.
ckp-sensor.fails: Cranks but will not start, stalls when hot then restarts after cooling, tach drops to zero while running.
ckp-sensor.tip: 1S7Z-6C315-AA. Cheap and common on Zetecs; the connector and wire near the block get brittle from heat, so check those too.

pcm.does: The engine computer: reads every sensor and controls fuel, spark, idle, the fan and, on automatics, shifting.
pcm.fails: No start with good crank and spark, several unrelated codes, or a scan tool that cannot talk to it; rare compared to sensors.
pcm.tip: Must be programmed to the VIN and the PATS keys relearned; a junkyard unit will not just plug in.

fuse-box.does: The engine bay box of fuses and relays that protects each circuit and switches big loads like the fan and fuel pump.
fuse-box.fails: One system dead (fan, pump, lights), a relay that clicks but does nothing, corroded terminals under the box.
fuse-box.tip: The lid shows the fuse map. Swap a suspect relay with an identical neighbor to test it; keep spare 10, 15 and 20 A fuses in the glovebox.

exh-mani.does: Cast header bolted to the head that collects hot exhaust, with the catalytic converter built into it to clean the gas.
exh-mani.fails: Ticking at cold start (cracked manifold or gasket), rotten-egg smell, P0420 code, loss of power from a clogged converter.
exh-mani.tip: 49-state and California versions differ; read the underhood emissions label. Studs snap when rusted, so soak them a day ahead.

flex-pipe.does: Front section of the exhaust with a braided flexible joint that lets the engine rock without cracking the pipes.
flex-pipe.fails: Sudden loud rasp under the front floor, exhaust smell in the cabin, sometimes a rattle from the torn braid.
flex-pipe.tip: A weld-in flex section is a cheap muffler-shop fix; the bolted assembly is the DIY route. New donut gasket while you are there.

muffler.does: Rear canister and tailpipe that cancel the exhaust noise before it leaves the car.
muffler.fails: Deep drone, rattle from loose baffles, rust holes, pipe hanging low on a broken hanger.
muffler.tip: The wagon muffler is a different part from sedan and hatch. Cut the old pipe if rusted; new clamps and rubber hangers are cheap.

mid-pipe.does: Middle section of the exhaust with a resonator chamber that cancels the annoying highway drone.
mid-pipe.fails: Hollow booming at cruise speed, rust weeping at the seams, rattle under the seats.
mid-pipe.tip: Usually replaced with the muffler as one cat-back. Check the rubber hangers; a sagging pipe tears the flex joint up front.

trans.does: Gearbox and differential in one case beside the engine: the MTX-75 5-speed stick or the 4F27E 4-speed automatic.
trans.fails: Manual: grinding into gear, popping out. Auto: harsh or delayed shifts, slipping, no reverse, whine that changes with speed.
trans.tip: Check fluid first: MTX-75 XT-M5-QS via the side fill plug, 4F27E MERCON V. A used 4F27E is the Mazda FN4A-EL if sourcing one.

clutch.does: Friction disc, pressure plate and release bearing that let you disconnect the engine from the manual gearbox to shift.
clutch.fails: Slipping (revs rise, speed does not), shudder on takeoff, chirp when the pedal is pressed, engagement high in the travel.
clutch.tip: Transaxle comes out, so do the rear main seal and release bearing at the same time. Bleed the hydraulic slave cylinder after.

cv-axle-l.does: Short driver-side driveshaft with two flexible joints that carries power from the transaxle to the left front wheel.
cv-axle-l.fails: Clicking on turns (outer joint), grease flung inside the wheel from a split boot, vibration on acceleration (inner joint).
cv-axle-l.tip: Axle nut is about 200 ft-lb, loosen with the wheel on the ground. Have a catch pan ready; the seal drips when the axle pops out.

cv-axle-r.does: Longer passenger-side driveshaft with an intermediate shaft and support bearing so both sides behave the same.
cv-axle-r.fails: Same click on turns and torn boots; the intermediate bearing adds a hum or growl that changes with speed, not turning.
cv-axle-r.tip: Three bolts hold the intermediate bearing bracket to the block. Buy the assembly with the shaft included; loosen the nut on the ground.

trans-fluid.does: The lubricant inside the transaxle: XT-M5-QS in the MTX-75 manual, MERCON V automatic fluid in the 4F27E.
trans-fluid.fails: Manual: notchy shifting, whine. Auto: burnt smell, brown fluid on the dipstick, slipping or harsh shifts.
trans-fluid.tip: MTX-75 takes XT-M5-QS through the side fill plug (about 2.2 qt), not gear oil. 4F27E: drain and fill MERCON V every 30k, no flush.

strut-fl.does: Left front leg that combines the shock, coil spring and top mount; the wheel steers by pivoting the whole strut.
strut-fl.fails: Bouncy ride, nose-dive under braking, clunk over bumps, oil wet on the strut body, cupped tire wear.
strut-fl.tip: Monroe 171505 loaded strut (LH) means no spring compressor. Replace as a pair with the right side and get an alignment after.

strut-fr.does: Right front leg that combines the shock, coil spring and top mount; the wheel steers by pivoting the whole strut.
strut-fr.fails: Same as the left: bounce, dive, clunks, leaking oil, cupped tires.
strut-fr.tip: Monroe 171504 loaded strut (RH). Do both sides together and mark the strut-to-knuckle bolts; they set camber.

lca-f.does: The lower arms that locate the bottom of each front knuckle, with a ball joint that lets the wheel steer and move.
lca-f.fails: Clunk over bumps, steering wander, popping when turning at low speed, uneven front tire wear.
lca-f.tip: Ball joint is pressed into the arm, so buy the arm complete. Torque the rear bushing bolt with the car on its wheels, then align.

sway-f.does: Thin links and rubber bushings that tie the front anti-roll bar to each strut so the car leans less in corners.
sway-f.fails: Rattle or clunk over small bumps at low speed that goes away when you press down on the corner of the car.
sway-f.tip: Most common front-end clunk on this car; 5S4Z-5K484-AA links, replace in pairs. Hold the stud with an Allen key while tightening.

shock-r.does: Two rear dampers and separate coil springs that control the rear of the wagon over bumps.
shock-r.fails: Rear end bouncing or wallowing, sagging under a load, thump over bumps, oil on the shock body.
shock-r.tip: Wagon shock and spring rates differ from sedan, so order for the ZTW. Shocks are a two-bolt job; springs need a compressor.

rear-blade.does: The multi-link rear arms; the long blade-shaped arm runs forward to a rubber body bushing that takes braking and bump loads.
rear-blade.fails: Clunk from the rear over bumps, rear end feels loose or steers itself over dips, uneven rear tire wear.
rear-blade.tip: The big front blade bushings are the known weak point. Bushings alone need a press; the whole arm bolts in, then align.

wheel-brg-f.does: Pressed-in bearings the front wheels spin on, sitting inside the knuckle behind the hub.
wheel-brg-f.fails: Hum or growl that rises with speed and changes when you swerve, play when you rock the wheel top to bottom.
wheel-brg-f.tip: Needs a shop press to swap the bearing into the knuckle. 6S4Z-1215-B supersedes YS4Z-1215-AA. Do not drive far on a howling one.

wheel-brg-r.does: Sealed bearings the rear wheels spin on; on drum-brake cars they live inside the drum hub.
wheel-brg-r.fails: Hum from the rear that changes when you weave, roughness when you spin the wheel by hand, wobble.
wheel-brg-r.tip: Dust cap, one big hub nut, and the drum or hub slides off the stub axle. Use a new nut and torque it; far easier than the fronts.

rotor-f.does: The 258mm vented steel discs the front pads squeeze; the vents let air cool them between stops.
rotor-f.fails: Steering wheel shake or pedal pulse when braking from speed (warped), grinding and deep grooves (worn out).
rotor-f.tip: Replace in pairs with fresh pads. Clean the hub face of rust so the new rotor sits flat; that is what causes most 'warping'.

pads-f.does: Friction blocks that clamp the front rotors; they do most of the car's stopping.
pads-f.fails: Squeal from the wear tab, grinding metal on metal, longer stops, brake dust heavier on one wheel.
pads-f.tip: Grease the caliper slide pins and shims when you change pads; sticky pins wear one pad early. Bed them in with gentle stops.

caliper-f.does: Hydraulic clamps at each front wheel that push the pads against the rotor when you brake.
caliper-f.fails: Pull to one side, one wheel hot or smelling after a drive, pad worn on one side only, fluid leak at the piston.
caliper-f.tip: Most 'bad calipers' are seized slide pins; clean and grease those first. If replacing, do both sides and bleed the brakes.

drum-r.does: The 203mm iron drums at the rear wheels; the shoes push out against the inside to slow the car.
drum-r.fails: Scraping from the back, weak parking brake, rear pulsing, a rust ridge that makes the drum hard to pull off.
drum-r.tip: Motorcraft BRD-45. Back off the adjuster through the slot if the drum will not come off. Rear-disc cars use a 253mm solid rotor instead.

shoes-r.does: Curved friction shoes, springs and the wheel cylinders that push them into the drum; also the parking brake.
shoes-r.fails: Grinding from the rear, parking brake weak or needs many clicks, fluid weep at the wheel cylinder, pedal sinking.
shoes-r.tip: Wagner Z764. Do one side at a time so you can copy the spring layout from the other. Replace leaking wheel cylinders with the shoes.

master-cyl.does: The cylinder your pedal pushes to make fluid pressure, with the vacuum booster behind it that multiplies your leg.
master-cyl.fails: Pedal slowly sinks at a stop (master), pedal hard as a rock with a hiss (booster), fluid low with no visible leak.
master-cyl.tip: Bench-bleed a new master before bolting it on. Flush the fluid every 2-3 years with DOT 3; dark fluid eats seals.

abs-mod.does: Pump and valve block that pulses brake pressure so the wheels keep rolling and steering during a panic stop.
abs-mod.fails: ABS light on, pedal buzz during normal stops, or a wheel locking early; usually a wheel speed sensor rather than the unit.
abs-mod.tip: 2M5Z-2C286-AA. Read the code first: a cheap wheel speed sensor is the usual cause. Needs a scan tool to bleed properly.

rack.does: Toothed bar in a housing under the engine that slides left or right as you turn the wheel, with power assist from the pump.
rack.fails: Fluid leaking from the boots, groan or extra effort turning, loose or notchy on-center feel, clunk from below.
rack.tip: Inner tie rods are part of the rack job. The subframe drops a bit; then a full alignment. Flush the old fluid when you fit it.

tie-rods.does: The outer ball joints that connect the steering rack to each front wheel's knuckle.
tie-rods.fails: Steering wander, clunk over bumps, play in the wheel, inner tire edge wear.
tie-rods.tip: Count the turns off the old one to keep toe close, then get an alignment. Replace in pairs; they are cheap.

ps-pump.does: Belt-driven hydraulic pump and its reservoir that supply the pressure that makes steering easy.
ps-pump.fails: Whine that rises when you turn, heavy steering at parking speed, foamy or low fluid, leak at the pump.
ps-pump.tip: Cardone 20-292 for 2000-03. Fill with MERCON V. Bleed by turning lock to lock with the front wheels off the ground before starting.

steering-col.does: The shaft from the steering wheel down to the rack, with a jointed intermediate shaft to get around the engine.
steering-col.fails: Clunk or click when turning at low speed, notchy feel, rattle from the column, airbag light if the clock spring is disturbed.
steering-col.tip: The intermediate shaft joints dry out; grease or replace. Column work means airbag: disconnect the battery and wait 10 minutes.

ac-comp.does: Belt-driven pump with an electromagnetic clutch that squeezes refrigerant to start the cooling cycle.
ac-comp.fails: A/C blows warm, clutch does not click on, grinding or squeal when A/C is switched on, belt slipping.
ac-comp.tip: If the clutch will not engage, check refrigerant level and the relay first. A swap needs evacuation and recharge equipment.

condenser.does: Thin radiator in front of the main radiator where hot refrigerant gives up its heat to outside air.
condenser.fails: A/C weakens in traffic and hot weather, oily stain on the fins from a leak, bent fins from road debris.
condenser.tip: Spectra 7-4879. Refrigerant must be recovered by a shop before you open the system. Fit a new receiver-drier at the same time.

blower.does: The cabin fan and the resistor pack that gives it four speeds.
blower.fails: Fan works only on high (resistor), no fan at all or squealing and slow (motor), burnt plastic smell.
blower.tip: Resistor is a couple of screws on the blower housing behind the glovebox; cheap fix. A clogged cabin filter overheats it.

heater-core.does: Small radiator behind the dash that engine coolant flows through to heat the cabin.
heater-core.fails: Sweet smell inside, windshield fogging, wet passenger floor, coolant loss, or no heat when the rest of the system is fine.
heater-core.tip: Known failure on this generation and a dash-out job. If it is only clogged, a garden-hose backflush through the heater hoses can restore heat.

cabin-filter.does: Paper filter that cleans outside air before the blower pushes it into the cabin.
cabin-filter.fails: Weak airflow at every fan speed, musty smell, dust on the vents.
cabin-filter.tip: Change yearly. On this car it sits under the hood in the passenger-side cowl beneath a plastic cover; the arrow shows airflow direction.

hood.does: The steel lid over the engine bay, hinged at the base of the windshield.
hood.fails: Will not latch or pops loose (cable or latch), rust along the leading edge, chips through to bare metal.
hood.tip: Have a helper when unbolting; scribe around the hinges so it goes back aligned. Grease the latch and check the release cable yearly.

front-bumper.does: The painted plastic skin over the front crash beam and lower grille.
front-bumper.fails: Cracks, sagging at the corners where tabs broke, missing clips, faded paint.
front-bumper.tip: Plastic push clips are cheap and go first; buy a bag. A dozen fasteners; a painted-to-match cover costs more than a raw one.

rear-bumper.does: The painted plastic skin at the back of the wagon, over the rear crash beam.
rear-bumper.fails: Scuffs from parking, corner tabs broken so it sags, cracks around the tow-hook hole.
rear-bumper.tip: Wagon rear cover is not the sedan or hatch part. Fasteners hide in the wheel wells and under the liftgate sill.

fender-l.does: The bolt-on panel over the left front wheel.
fender-l.fails: Rust at the bottom rear corner behind the wheel liner, dents, paint bubbling.
fender-l.tip: Pull the plastic wheel liner first and dig out the mud that rots the corner. Bolts run along the door jamb and under the hood edge.

fender-r.does: The bolt-on panel over the right front wheel (Partslink FO1241210).
fender-r.fails: Rust at the lower rear corner, dents, mismatched paint from an old repair.
fender-r.tip: Same as the left: clean out the liner pocket. A painted-to-match fender saves the body shop step.

door-fl.does: Driver door shell with hinges and check strap; holds the window, regulator, latch and mirror.
door-fl.fails: Sag that makes it drop into the striker, rust along the bottom seam, clicking check strap, loose hinge pins.
door-fl.tip: Heavy, and the wiring loom runs through the jamb boot: two people and a floor jack with a towel. Grease the hinges twice a year.

door-fr.does: Front passenger door shell with hinges and check strap; holds its window, regulator and latch.
door-fr.fails: Sag, rust along the bottom, worn check strap, rattling inner panel.
door-fr.tip: Same handling as the driver door. Swap the interior panel, glass and latch over from the old door if you fit a used shell.

door-rl.does: Left rear door shell; holds the rear window regulator, latch and child lock.
door-rl.fails: Rust at the bottom edge, window grinding as the regulator fails, latch not catching.
door-rl.tip: Rear doors are lighter but still a two-person job. The child lock lever is in the latch edge; check it before blaming the latch.

door-rr.does: Right rear door shell; holds the rear window regulator, latch and child lock.
door-rr.fails: Rust, dents from parking-lot doors, window slow or stuck, latch not catching.
door-rr.tip: Same as the left rear. Rear regulators are Dorman 741-584/585 if the glass drops while you are in there.

liftgate.does: The wagon's rear hatch, hinged at the roof, with two gas struts that hold it up.
liftgate.fails: Hatch falls or will not stay up, worse in cold weather; rust at the lower seam; rear wiper or lock quits when the loom chafes.
liftgate.tip: StrongArm 4358 struts (interchange YS41-N406A10-A). Pop the clips with a small screwdriver and swap one at a time with a helper holding it.

windshield.does: Laminated safety glass glued into the body; it braces the roof and backs up the passenger airbag.
windshield.fails: Cracks spreading from chips, wiper haze, whistle or water leak from a bad urethane seal.
windshield.tip: Fill chips right away; once a crack crosses your sight line, replace. Glass shops come to you and insurance often waives the deductible.

roof.does: The welded steel panel spanning the pillars; part of the car's structure.
roof.fails: Rust bubbles along the drip rails and roof rack mounts, dents from hail, clear coat peeling.
roof.tip: Replacement means cutting and welding, so body shop only. Keep the roof rail channels clean so water does not sit and start rust.

mirrors.does: The two door mirrors, manually or electrically adjusted, each with a glass and a housing.
mirrors.fails: Glass loose or fallen out, mirror will not adjust, housing cracked from a garage clip.
mirrors.tip: Dorman 955-020 (LH) / 955-021 (RH). Three nuts behind the triangle trim inside the door; glass alone can be replaced with adhesive.

wipers.does: Front wiper blades and the motor that drives the wagon's rear wiper.
wipers.fails: Streaks and chatter (blades); rear wiper slow, stopping mid-sweep or parking wrong (motor or wiring in the liftgate boot).
wipers.tip: Front blades snap on; change yearly. Rear motor is behind the liftgate trim; check the rubber loom boot for chafed wires first.

headlamp-l.does: Left headlamp housing with reflector, lens and the 9007 bulb for low and high beam.
headlamp-l.fails: Yellowed, hazy lens that dims the beam, moisture inside, cracked mounting tab, misaimed beam.
headlamp-l.tip: Try a lens restoration kit before replacing. Two bolts on top and one behind the corner; aim the beam on a wall afterward.

headlamp-r.does: Right headlamp housing with reflector, lens and the 9007 bulb for low and high beam.
headlamp-r.fails: Same as the left: haze, moisture, broken tabs, dim beam.
headlamp-r.tip: Replace as a pair so color and brightness match. Do not touch the glass of a new bulb; skin oil shortens its life.

taillamp-l.does: Left wagon tail lamp housing with the 3157 tail/brake and turn bulbs.
taillamp-l.fails: One bulb out, cracked lens letting water in, corroded socket causing a fast-flash turn signal.
taillamp-l.tip: 2S4Z-13405-AA. Reached from inside the cargo area behind the trim panel; two nuts. Clean the socket contacts with a pencil eraser.

taillamp-r.does: Right wagon tail lamp housing with the 3157 tail/brake and turn bulbs.
taillamp-r.fails: Bulb out, water inside the lens, corroded socket, fast-flash turn signal.
taillamp-r.tip: TYC 11-5963-01 / 2S4Z-13404-AA. Same two nuts behind the cargo trim; push the lamp out from behind.

bulbs.does: The three bulb types that light the car: 9007 headlamps, 3157 tail/brake/turn, 194 side markers and small lamps.
bulbs.fails: One lamp dark, fast-flashing turn signal, dim yellowed headlights.
bulbs.tip: Replace headlamp bulbs in pairs and handle by the base only. Keep a spare 3157 and 194 in the glovebox; a fast flasher means a dead bulb.

seat-fl.does: Driver's seat and the track that lets it slide and, with the side lever, change height.
seat-fl.fails: Seat rocks on the track, height lever loose, torn bolster, seat belt warning from a bad buckle connector.
seat-fl.tip: Four bolts to the floor, then unplug the buckle sensor. Disconnect the battery first: the airbag system reads the seat belt buckle.

seat-fr.does: Front passenger seat on its track.
seat-fr.fails: Rocking on the track, torn fabric, airbag warning light from a chafed connector underneath.
seat-fr.tip: Same four bolts. A used seat from a sedan fits the wagon; match the cloth and any side airbag option.

seat-rear.does: The split 60/40 rear bench that folds flat to make the wagon a cargo hauler.
seat-rear.fails: Latch will not release, cushion loose, folding hinge stiff, seat belt buckle cover cracked.
seat-rear.tip: The bottom cushion pops up on two clips; the fuel pump access is under it. Vacuum the hinge tracks so the seatback folds smoothly.

dash.does: The instrument cluster that shows speed, revs, fuel and temperature, plus the warning lights the PCM turns on.
dash.fails: Gauges sweep or drop to zero (cracked solder joints), dim or dead backlight bulbs, odometer segments missing.
dash.tip: 2M5Z-10849-DA. Behind the bezel and two screws; a used one carries its own mileage, so a rebuild service is the clean route.

window-reg.does: Cable and motor mechanism inside each door that raises and lowers the glass.
window-reg.fails: Window drops into the door, grinding or a pop when you press the switch, glass tilted in the track.
window-reg.tip: This car's signature failure. Dorman 741-874/875 front, 741-584/585 rear. Tape the glass up before removing the old regulator.

door-latch.does: The mechanical latch in each door and the electric actuator that locks and unlocks it from the fob or switch.
door-latch.fails: One door will not lock or unlock with the others, handle does nothing, door opens while driving, latch rattles.
door-latch.tip: Latch and actuator come as one assembly; three Torx screws in the door edge. Lube the striker and latch with white grease yearly.

shifter.does: The gear lever and the two cables that run through the floor to move the transaxle's shift mechanism.
shifter.fails: Sloppy or stiff shifting, will not go into a gear, lever loose, auto not showing the right gear in the cluster.
shifter.tip: Cable end bushings wear and pop off; that is the usual manual-shifter complaint. Auto: check cable adjustment before blaming the 4F27E.

key.does: The PATS transponder key with a chip the ignition reads, and the fob that locks and unlocks the doors.
key.fails: Theft light flashes rapidly and the engine cranks but will not run (chip not read); fob range shrinks or dies (battery).
key.tip: Fob CWTWB1U331 takes a CR2032. With two working keys you can program a third yourself; with one, you need a locksmith or dealer.

wheel-fl.does: Front left 15-inch wheel with a 195/60R15 tire; it steers and drives.
wheel-fl.fails: Vibration through the wheel (balance), inside-edge wear (alignment), cracked sidewall, bent rim from a pothole.
wheel-fl.tip: Rotate front to rear every 5-7k miles; the fronts wear faster. Torque lugs to 94 ft-lb in a star pattern, not with an impact gun.

wheel-fr.does: Front right 15-inch wheel with a 195/60R15 88H tire; it steers and drives.
wheel-fr.fails: Vibration, edge wear, bent rim; the passenger side eats more curb and pothole damage.
wheel-fr.tip: Same size and torque as the left. Check pressure monthly, about 32 psi cold; the sticker is on the driver door jamb.

wheel-rl.does: Rear left 15-inch wheel with a 195/60R15 tire; it follows and brakes.
wheel-rl.fails: Cupped tread if a shock is bad; a slow leak from a corroded steel rim bead is common.
wheel-rl.tip: Rears wear slowly, so rotate them forward. A cupped rear tire means look at the shocks and Control Blade bushings.

wheel-rr.does: Rear right 15-inch wheel with a 195/60R15 tire; it follows and brakes.
wheel-rr.fails: Cupping, slow leak, or a hum that is really a wheel bearing.
wheel-rr.tip: Same as the rear left. Keep all four the same brand and tread depth so the ABS sees matched wheel speeds.

lugs.does: Twenty M12x1.5 nuts that hold the four wheels on, plus the spare tire under the cargo floor.
lugs.fails: Rounded or swollen lug nuts the socket no longer fits, seized studs, a spare that is flat when you need it.
lugs.tip: Torque 94 ft-lb in a star pattern. Check the spare's pressure twice a year and keep the jack and wrench in the cargo well.
